messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris, a couple things here:

1) You need to initialize 'kdqf' before you assign into a subset of
it, using numeric() (aka nimNumeric()).
Otherwise NIMBLE can't figure out its size.
Not sure if that's the only issue as I would need code for your model
to reproduce this. But please start there
and then respond if that doesn't solve the problem.

2) More generally, as you note, that error message seems misleading.
If you can provide a reproducible example (either your
full model, or ideally a simplified version that just focuses on the
error that is occurring), we can
take a look and see if we can figure out why the message occurs when
it does and if we can improve that.

chris

> kron_diag_quad_form <- nimbleFunction(
>   run = function(L = double(2), diag = double(3)){
>     returnType(double(2))
>     diag_dim <- dim(diag)
>     T <- diag_dim[2]
>     K <- diag_dim[3]
>     KT <- K*T
>     kdqf <- matrix(double(0, KT^2, init=FALSE), ncol=T)
>
>     for (kr in 1:K){
>       kr_step <- (kr-1)*T
>       for (kc in 1:(kr-1)){
>         kc_step <- (kc-1)*T
>         kdqf_sub <- L[kr,kr] * L[kr,kc] * diag[1:T,1:T,kr]

>           kdqf_sub <- kdqf_sub + L[kj,kr] * L[kj,kc] * diag[1:T,1:T,kj]

messages.subject: Re: dimension mismatch in variable
messages.body_plain:
Two issues.  First, you need full indexing on the matrix W in the model, specifically in chol(W).

Second, to get the model to build without an error about chol() of a singular matrix, then provide initial values for W and I_K, through the "inits" list argument.  Easiest choice is identity matrix.

Both changes shown below, works fine:

library(nimble)

nimble_Wish_code <- nimbleCode({
    W[1:K,1:K] ~ dwish(R = I_K[1:K,1:K], df = K + 1)

    Li_K[1:K,1:K] <- chol(W[1:K,1:K])

})

NIMBLE_model <- nimbleModel(
    nimble_Wish_code,

    constants = list( K = 15 ),
    inits = list( I_K = diag(15), W = diag(15) )
)

messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris, this doesn't look like anything related to NIMBLE but rather
with your model structure.

Considering just your K=1 case (the K>1 should be similar)...

When you have:
B[m] ~ dnorm(mean=B_hat,sd=1000)

you're basically saying that the B[m] values can be very far from
B_hat. Given this wide variance, you can't learn much about B_hat.
Even if your data could pin down each B[m] without any uncertainty,
you only have 7 B[m] values to try to learn about B_hat in a situation
where you say with certainty that the signal to noise ratio is very
low (sd=1000).

Given the normality here, we know analytically that the posterior
variance for B_hat is 1 / (1/1000^2 + 7/1000^2) = 125000 (e.g., see
Gelman et al Bayesian data analysis book, section 2.5).

The standard model structure here would be to have something like:
B[m] ~ dnorm(mean=B_hat,sd=tau)
and put a prior on tau  (e.g., tau ~ dunif(0, some_big_value)) or a
half-Cauchy distribution). That way you can learn how close the B[m]
values are to the B_hat based on the data.  And then, presuming that
tau is not estimated to be too large, you'll be able to learn about
B_hat from what you can learn about the B[m] values.

Side note: you don't really need inverse(). You can just do:
A_hat <- diag(x=rep(1/1000,K))
And in fact since A_hat is constant, you could just initialize it
outside the model and pass it in as either 'inits' or 'constants'.
Doesn't matter much with small K and because A_hat is never updated in
the MCMC, but just a note.

Second side note: I would not initialize A inside the loop, since it
is not indexed by 'm'. The result is that you are asking nimble to
create the same node multiple times. Doesn't cause a problem here, but
it could lead to problems in other situations.

Chris

messages.body_plain:
So far multivariate MRF spatial models have had limited development within Nimble. Some possibilities exist to construct multi models from independent CAR models, but these have not been publically offered as yet (as far as this author is aware). As an alternative a relatively simple but sophisticated approach to multi models is the latent structure M-models of Martinez-Beneito et al (2017). In their formulation the multivariate spatial model is formed by a convex combination of independent CAR and UH models. The code for these models are available in OpenBUGS and in Nimble format (attached). Both code forms have been posted on the GitHub repository: https://github.com/Andrew9Lawson/Bayesian-DM-code-examples,
 under the branch 'Multi-models'  for the Georgia county level data on asthma, COPD and angina.

Reference:
Martinez-Beneito, Miguel A.; Botella-Rocamora, Paloma; Banerjee, Sudipto. Towards a Multidimensional Approach to Bayesian Disease Mapping. Bayesian Anal. 12 (2017), no. 1, 239--259. doi:10.1214/16-BA995. https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.ba/1458324098

I'm a recent user of nimble, I was working on a simple linear multivariate model on a machine that had the 0.6-11 version of nimble.

'Error: Failed to create the shared library'

See below the model's code

model_nimble2 <- nimbleCode({

   ## Priors

  sigma~dunif(0,10)
  tau <- pow(sigma,-2)

  sigma_pred~dunif(0,100)
  tau_pred <- pow(sigma_pred,-2)

  beta0 ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
  beta0_pred ~ dnorm(0,0.01)

  for(k in 1:K){
    beta[k] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
    beta_pred[k] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
  }

  for (i in 1:n_reading){
    Dat[i,10]~ dnorm(mu[i], tau)
    mu[i] <-  beta0 + beta[1] * Dat[i,8] +
      beta[2] * Dat[i,11] + beta[3] * Dat[i,12]

    ## Predict the True length based only on covariates available in "normal" conditions
       Dat_pred[i,8] ~ dnorm(mu_pred[i], tau_pred)
    mu_pred[i] <- beta0_pred + beta_pred[1] * Dat_pred[i,10] + beta_pred[2] * Dat_pred[i,11] +
      beta_pred[3] * Dat_pred[i,12]

  }
  ## END model
}

)

Constants are entered as follow (Dat is a data frame

nimble_data <- list(K=K,
                    n_fish=n_fish,
                    n_reading=n_reading ,
                    fish_r=fish_r,
                    Dat=Dat,
                    Dat_pred = Dat,
                    mu=rep(0,n_reading),
                    mu_pred=rep(0,n_reading)
)

Thanks in advance for any help/suggestion

G
